parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no birth-sex facility rules, no documented police sweeps, border friction, or custody-placement rules reaching visitors. The dossier's negatives are largely resident-sphere: onerous marker-change processes (irrelevant to a visitor's home passport), deep stigma, and documented discrimination plus physical/sexual harassment of visibly trans people in a provincial city (2024) and severe rural violence against residents. Those are tier-3 societal-hostility signals, not documented targeting of travellers, but they are real and current rather than absent. Climate negatives include a head of government's homophobic video (2026) with supporters' death threats and rising anti-LGBT sentiment — raising the severity of everyday encounters. Positives: protective judicial framework, civil-society infrastructure with 50+ branches, pride events, curriculum inclusion. Thin on visitor-specific axes (border treatment, detention placement, HRT access) — open questions, not exposures. This sits at the reduced-risk band, comparable to a jurisdiction with no visitor-facing restrictions but recurring documented hostility and only partial remedies; not lower, because nothing visitor-facing is documented as enforced against travellers.
